description: GCT USB4105 USB Type-C receptacle for USB 2.0, SMT, PCB top mount, horizontal: 16 contacts (GND, VBUS, CC1/CC2, D+/D- on both sides, SBU1/SBU2) plus a grounded stainless steel shell with four through-board stakes. VBUS 5 A and GND 6.25 A collectively, 48 V DC, 240 W, 20,000 mating cycles, -40 to 85 C. Gold flash contacts, tape and reel, 0.95 mm stakes. 8.94 x 7.35 x 3.31 mm.

metadata.body_mm: 8.94 wide x 7.35 deep x 3.31 high above the seating plane; tails 0.38 behind the body (7.73 overall depth)
metadata.mounting_method: surface_mount, top mount, horizontal; shell stakes through the board
metadata.packaging: tape and reel, 800 pcs per reel, 24.0 mm tape
metadata.weight_source: LCSC unit weight (distributor); GCT states no mass

params.note: Stainless steel shell, nickel plated; four stakes through the board (S = 0.95 ±0.15 mm below the seating plane for the blank stake suffix). The pin table assigns it to GND.
params.source: https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf (pin table, Material, Plating, side view, ordering grid)

params.note: USB Type-C positions A1-A12, B1-B12; the drawing's pin table has only the 16 USB 2.0 contacts, so A2, A3, A10, A11, B2, B3, B10 and B11 are unused. GND and VBUS mate first, CC, D and SBU second. Mating force 5-20 N, unmating 8-20 N (6-20 N after 20,000 cycles), 20,000 cycles. Opening 8.34 (+0.06/-0.02) x 2.56 ±0.04 mm on an axis 1.73 mm above the board. Sources: GCT drawing USB4105 rev B4 (pin table, front and side views), GCT specification rev A3 §6.2.

Case opening: a mated plug's overmold is at most 6.5 mm high and stays at least 1.85 mm in front of the receptacle face, so a wall in front of J1 thicker than that keeps the plug from seating fully when the receptacle face is flush with the wall's inside.
params.source: https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf (Plug and Receptacle Mating View)

interfaces.name: Solder tails, shell stakes and locating pegs (SMT, top mount)

params.note: 16 surface-mount tails 0.20 mm wide at 0.50 mm pitch (4 pairs in 0.45 mm groups, 6.40 mm outer span) ending 0.38 mm behind the body; 4 shell stakes on 8.64 mm through the board, front pair 2.60 mm behind the mating face, rear pair 4.18 mm further back, 0.80 / 1.10 mm wide; 2 plastic locating pegs Ø0.50 mm on 5.78 mm, 3.68 mm behind the front stakes, 0.60 mm below the seating plane. Coplanarity 0.10 mm. Mount with the mating face at the board edge (the drawing's layout shows the PCB edge under the front).
params.source: https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf (bottom, side, front and rear views; recommended PCB layout)

params.note: Lead-free reflow: peak 255 C (-0/+5), 60 s above 217 C, 50 s above 230 C, 5 s above 250 C, soak 2-3 min, ramp 2.5 C/s, cooling 5 C/s max.
params.source: https://gct.co/files/specs/usb4105-spec.pdf (§7.0)

name: GCT USB4105-GF-A USB-C receptacle (USB 2.0, top mount)

params.standard: USB Type-C receptacle, USB 2.0 contacts only

params.note: Ordering code USB4105-XX-A-XXX: XX = contact plating (GF gold flash, standard; 15 or 30 u" gold); A = tape and reel; XXX = shell stake length (blank 0.95 mm, 060 0.60 mm, 120 1.20 mm). This part is the blank (0.95 mm) stake. JLCPCB stocks the -060 and -120 variants as separate parts.
GCT's product page could not be read (Cloudflare challenge). LCSC lists C3020560 with product cycle "normal"; JLCPCB had 11,505 in stock on 2026-10-03.

params.resolution: Manufacturer: 16 contacts, each a leaf. The distributors count the 12 tail groups: A1/B12, A4/B9, B4/A9 and B1/A12 each share a 0.45 mm group.

params.note: GCT's drawing and specification state no mass; weight_g is LCSC's unit weight (0.68 g).

GCT links its 3D models from its product page, which answers every fetch with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), as do guessed STEP paths under gct.co/files/. SnapEDA and Ultra Librarian need a login and forbid redistribution. The community KiCad model is CC-BY-SA 4.0 and would bring share-alike terms into this library; not used. Geometry is generated from drawing USB4105 rev B4 (library/cad/py/catalog/gct-usb4105-gf-a.py).

params.reason: The pin table gives a D+ and a D- contact on each side and the specification rotates the plug 180° in its durability test, but neither GCT source says how a USB 2.0 board wires them. Joining the pairs, so either plug orientation reaches the USB device, is USB Type-C practice and is not cited here.
source: https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf (sheet 1 pin table: Pin, Signal, Mating Sequence)
params.value: the board joins A6 (Dp1) with B6 (Dp2) and A7 (Dn1) with B7 (Dn2)

params.reason: The drawing dimensions the outline (8.94 x 7.35 x 3.31), axis height (1.73), opening, stake and peg positions and tail positions, but not the shell wall, cavity depth, tongue, stake thickness or tail foot; the representative model needs single values, scaled from the drawing's views.
params.source: https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf
params.value: outer shell a stadium 8.94 x 3.16 mm (0.30 mm wall around the 8.34 x 2.56 opening, bottom 0.15 mm above the seating plane) over the full 7.35 mm depth; cavity 4.85 mm deep; tongue 6.78 x 0.70 mm from 0.30 mm behind the face; stakes 0.30 mm thick centred on the 8.64 mm line; tail feet 0.75 mm long x 0.10 mm thick, pair tails 0.05 mm apart in their 0.45 mm group
